lines.trans: Doctor, wait a minute, please!
What is the matter, sweetie? Does something hurt you?
My tank broke.
Can you fix it?
A tank? Let me see.
No, buddy, I cannot fix tanks.
I only treat people, after all.
And can the state fix a tank?
Now a tank — the state certainly can fix that!
For tanks the state always has money.
Thank you, Doctor! I will try to fix it myself.
Go to your mama, sweetie! Don't be sad.

meanings.note: Contrast. Core Russian conj meaning 'and, but; so' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.en: to be ill, to be sick
meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be ill', paired with 'заболеть'.

examples.text: Я этого не хочу. Но вспомни, у тебя сын болеет.
examples.trans: I don't want that. But remember, your son is ill.

meanings.note: Male sibling. Common masculine noun meaning 'brother, cousin' in everyday Russian.
in двоюродный/троюродный брат, often shortened to брат

examples.text: Мой старший брат живёт в Москве.
examples.trans: My older brother lives in Moscow.

examples.text: А это брат Всеволод. Мы очень переживаем.
examples.trans: And this is cousin Vsevolod. We're very worried.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Present есть; у меня есть = I have. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: Adds a reason or an obvious truth. Core Russian part meaning 'after all, you know' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I did tell you, you know!

examples.text: Садись, не бойся. Я ведь сам чуть тебя не отпустил.
examples.trans: Sit down, don't be afraid. I very nearly let you go myself.

meanings.note: Pointing at something. Core Russian part meaning 'here, there (pointing)' in everyday speech.
Emphasis. Core Russian part meaning 'here, there (pointing)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'егда').

examples.trans: She's offended. She's always like that.

meanings.note: Neuter noun in -о. Common neuter noun meaning 'state, country' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The state will reimburse you the money later.
The state takes care of citizens.

examples.text: Государство обязательно увидит и назначит операцию.
examples.trans: The state will surely see and will schedule the surgery.

meanings.note: Intransitive. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be sad, grieve', paired with 'погрустить'.

examples.text: Иди к маме, малыш! Не грусти.
examples.trans: Go to your mama, sweetie! Don't be sad.
Don't be sad, everything will be fine.

examples.text: Привет всем! Что вы тут грустите?
examples.trans: Hello everyone! Why are you sad here?

meanings.note: plural only: there is no singular in everyday use

examples.trans: The money is on the table.
Gum? I didn't have enough money.

meanings.note: medical practitioner; often used as form of address

examples.trans: Doctor, I urgently need a cast.
It hurts, it hurts! It hurts very much, Doctor!

examples.text: Я умоляю вас, доктор! Это всё ради любви!
examples.trans: I beg you, Doctor! This is all for love!

meanings.note: In one direction, now. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to go (on foot)', paired with 'пойти'.
To run for a second term. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to go (on foot)', paired with 'пойти'.

examples.trans: He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: + dative. Core Russian prep meaning 'to, towards' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: There's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.note: Врач лечит больных. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to treat (a patient); (slang) to lecture', paired with 'вылечить'.

meanings.en: (colloquial) to lecture, to try to talk round
meanings.note: не надо меня лечить = don't lecture me

examples.trans: This doctor treats patients very well.

examples.text: Не надо меня лечить, хорошо? Я своё решение принял.
examples.trans: Don't lecture me, alright? I've made my decision.

meanings.note: affectionate; also said to a child as 'kid'

examples.text: Послушай, малыш, у меня есть деловое предложение.
examples.trans: Listen, kid, I've got a business proposal.

meanings.note: мам! = casual 'Mum!' when calling her
friendly diminutive of 'минута'; 'на минутку' = for a minute

examples.trans: Let me have it for a minute.

examples.text: Соседи, привет! Слушай, дружок, дай свой телефон на минутку.
examples.trans: Hi, neighbours! Listen, buddy, lend me your phone for a minute.

meanings.note: + infinitive. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'can, to be able', paired with 'смочь'.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: + prepositional: на сайте. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.
+ accusative: на второй срок. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
+ genitive: 'у нас нет выбора' = we have no choice
+ genitive. Core Russian part meaning 'no; there isn't' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: come on, go on, let's see
meanings.note: Informal, before a command. Core Russian part meaning 'come on, go on' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Go on, tell me: how much is here?

meanings.note: Подожди! = wait!. Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'ождать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to wait (a while)', paired with 'ждать'.

examples.text: Подожди, Нин, ты не поняла. Это же стыдно!
examples.trans: Wait, Nina, you don't get it. It's shameful!

meanings.note: Handing something over. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'жалуйста').
Answer to thanks. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'жалуйста').
Handing something over. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'жалуйста').
Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to show', paired with 'показывать'.

examples.trans: Shall we show this to Anikeev?

examples.text: Ну, покажите руки. Что у вас за спиной?
examples.trans: Well, show me your hands. What is behind your back?

meanings.en: to try, to taste (food or drink)
meanings.note: + accusative. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'пробовать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to try, to taste', paired with 'пробовать'.

+ infinitive. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'пробовать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to try, to taste', paired with 'пробовать'.

examples.trans: Try the tea with bread rings.

meanings.note: + acc. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'чинить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to fix, repair', paired with 'чинить'.

examples.trans: I will try to fix it myself.
And can the state fix a tank?

meanings.note: Сам, сама, само, сами. Core Russian pron meaning 'oneself (myself, yourself...)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

meanings.note: Intransitive, reflexive. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ломаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to break down, get broken', paired with 'ломаться'.

examples.trans: Yesterday the washing machine broke down.

meanings.note: спасибо за + accusative = thank you for

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: 'что я за мэр такой' = what kind of mayor am I
Core Russian pron meaning 'such, like this' in everyday speech.
